data.hook: Right after a dominant season-opening win in Australia, the 49ers revealed they'd quietly locked in their star coach for years ahead.
data.name: 49ers Extend Kyle Shanahan's Contract After Offseason Deal
data.summary: The San Francisco 49ers signed head coach Kyle Shanahan to a contract extension during the offseason, extending beyond his previous deal through 2027. The news, first reported by Tom Pelissero, came just after their 27-7 victory over the Rams in Melbourne to open the 2026 season. Fans expressed relief and praise for Shanahan's leadership, which has delivered six playoff runs, two NFC titles, and two Super Bowl appearances since 2017. The move brings stability and shuts down earlier doubts about his future.

data.hook: Myles Garrett stepped onto the field in Melbourne for his first game with the Rams, but a nagging knee issue held him back from the start.
data.name: Myles Garrett Struggles in Rams Debut Against 49ers
data.summary: The star edge rusher recorded zero tackles, sacks, or QB hits as the Rams lost 27-7 to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. Fresh off a trade from the Browns and battling knee swelling from training camp, Garrett called it the worst version of himself and focused on recovery over forcing plays. Trent Williams shut him down completely, though some noted Garrett's hurries in advanced stats and the tough matchup while not at full strength.

data.hook: Fred Warner chased down plays all night in Melbourne, then etched his name in franchise history with the tackle that passed Patrick Willis.
data.name: Warner Sets 49ers Tackle Record in Australia Blowout Win Over Rams
data.summary: The San Francisco 49ers kicked off the 2026 NFL season with a 27-7 rout of the Los Angeles Rams in the league's first regular-season game at Melbourne Cricket Ground, drawing over 100,000 fans. Linebacker Fred Warner shone brightest, recording 11 tackles—including a forced fumble and pass breakup—to earn PFF's top defensive grade of 91.1 so far, while passing Hall of Famer Patrick Willis as the 49ers' all-time leading tackler and receiving the game ball from coach Kyle Shanahan. Brock Purdy tossed three touchdown passes, the defense stifled Matthew Stafford, and new Rams rusher Myles Garrett managed zero tackles in a quiet debut hampered by a knee issue.

data.hook: Two NFL teams flew 15 hours to Melbourne, but victory hinged on who cracked the jet lag code best. The 49ers settled in early; the Rams dashed in last-minute with a science-backed plan.
data.name: 49ers Dominate Rams in NFL's Australia Debut Amid Jet Lag Battle
data.summary: The San Francisco 49ers beat the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 in the NFL's first regular-season game at Melbourne Cricket Ground, drawing over 100,000 fans. The 49ers arrived a week early to adjust to the 17-hour time difference, while the Rams used a quick 'in-and-out' trip, staying on Pacific Time with a plane full of lay-flat beds and two years of staff testing. Brock Purdy threw three touchdown passes in the win, sparking talk on which travel method worked better, though one game leaves questions open for the NFL's global push.

data.hook: Fresh off a season-ending ankle injury, Fred Warner flew around the field in Melbourne, Australia, racking up tackles and forcing fumbles like he never missed a beat.
data.name: Fred Warner Dominates in 49ers' Win Over Rams, Drops Hilarious Instagram Post
data.summary: In the San Francisco 49ers' 27-7 season-opening rout of the Los Angeles Rams, Warner tallied 11 tackles, a pass deflection, and a forced fumble, passing Hall of Famer Patrick Willis for most tackles in franchise history and Charles Haley for forced fumbles. The 29-year-old teamed with Dre Greenlaw on a key play and anchored a goal-line stand that sealed the win. Post-game, his Instagram carousel captioned 'Google Me' jabbed at the Rams and included a clip of romance scammer Daejon Love, drawing laughs and fresh debates on his elite linebacker status amid All-Pro honors and a top PFF grade.

data.hook: During the 49ers' season opener in Australia, fans flooded timelines with highlights of Daejon Love—a wide receiver who never existed—complete with injury reports and betting props.
data.name: Fake 49ers Player Daejon Love Becomes NFL Meme Sensation
data.summary: Daejon Love, a 35-year-old California man arrested in late August for federal wire fraud, allegedly posed as a 49ers player to scam 26 women out of $1.3 million in fake romance schemes. Social media turned the story into a fictional NFL saga, with memes of Love leading the team tunnel walk, getting carted off injured, and even NBA star Tyrese Haliburton wearing a custom jersey joking he's on IR. The 49ers coach and players joined the fun, while the real team beat the Rams 27-7 amid the online buzz.

data.hook: A Dolphins fan flying to Vegas had a blunt take on the season opener: 'None.' Now Clelin Ferrell gets a shot at the Raiders who once drafted him fourth overall.
data.name: Dolphins Elevate Clelin Ferrell for Raiders Opener Amid Rebuild
data.summary: The Miami Dolphins called up edge rusher Clelin Ferrell from the practice squad to face the Las Vegas Raiders in their season opener at Allegiant Stadium. The former first-round pick out of Clemson brings 21 career sacks and veteran depth to a young defense, creating a personal revenge storyline against his original team. Entering a full rebuild with new GM Jon-Eric Sullivan, coach Jeff Hafley, and QB Malik Willis, the Dolphins face low expectations—including talk of an 0-17 season—making this a key test for the regime. Kickoff is 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX, with Miami as underdogs.

data.hook: The Vikings head into their heated rivalry game with every player ready to go, while the Packers nurse key injury doubts just hours from kickoff.
data.name: Healthy Vikings Face Injured Packers in NFC North Opener
data.summary: Minnesota enters Sunday's season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium with no injury designations, confirming left tackle Christian Darrisaw and safety Harrison Smith are good after rest days. The Vikings elevated outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy and running back DeeJay Dallas from the practice squad for expected playing time. Green Bay lists guard Aaron Banks, tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, and linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper as questionable, with defensive tackle Warren Brinson out due to a calf injury; they elevated wide receiver Bo Melton and linebacker Kristian Welch. Fans on both sides buzz with optimism ahead of the 132nd meeting at 3:25 p.m. CT on CBS.
